text: The heart of the nomadic settlement, growing from a scattering of tents to the seat of a steppe king.
The horde does not build walls; it builds strength.
Felt-workers whose skill houses the whole horde, and cheapens every camp raised beside them.
A home that folds by morning and stands by dusk.
Wagon-builders whose carts carry the horde further with every season.
The steppe is endless; good wheels make it smaller.
Wool and felt spun into goods prized far beyond the grasslands.
From goat hair and patience, wealth is spun.
Hardy flocks that feed the camp through the cruellest winters.
Milk, meat and hair - the goat wastes nothing.
Sheep are the coin of the steppe, driven to market on the hoof.
Count a man's sheep and you have counted his silver.
Communal hearths where armies provision before the long ride.
Around the fire, the host eats, mends and readies for war.
Fermented mare's milk and imported wine, sold at handsome profit.
Open grounds where caravans meet the horde and every deal favours the host.
No coin needed - a horse for a bride, a hide for a blade.
Tale-keepers whose memory holds the learning of the steppe.
Wisdom rides from mouth to ear, faster than any horse.
Every recruit rides out already blooded by the veterans of these yurts.
Born in the saddle, raised by the bow.
A travelling forge arming the khan's chosen with blades and scale.
Steppe iron is quenched in mare's milk and vengeance.
Craftsmen of the composite bow, pride of every nomad general.
Horn, birch and sinew - a bow that outranges empires.
Steppe nobility whose oversight enriches all and suffers no thieving hands.
Where the noyans camp, order follows the herds.
Tallies of plunder and tribute, counted to the last horsehair.
Tribute is the harvest of fear well sown.
Shamans read the sky's favour, calming hearts and steadying the camp.
The Sky sees all; the horde is at peace beneath it.
Endless drilling at the gallop makes the horde's riders cheap to raise and deadly in the charge.
Ride before you walk; shoot before you speak.
Prime grazing lands that fatten the herds and fill the camp's stores.
Grass is the gold of the steppe.
Riders muster here for raids beyond the frontier - profitable, swift and despised by every neighbour.
What the steppe does not give, the borderlands will.
The heart of the nomadic settlement.
Industry of the steppe: felt, wagons and wool.
Flocks, herds and hearths that feed the horde.
Barter, drink and tales traded across the grasslands.
Warriors, forges and bowyers of the horde.
Nobles, tribute and the favour of the Eternal Sky.
Roads, hunting lodges and watchtowers of the Korean frontier.
